title: Eye Tracking for the Assessment of Learning Performance in Children and Adolescents with Seizures and a Healthy Control Group
summary:
Epilepsy is one of the most common chronic neurological disorders in childhood and adolescence and is frequently associated with cognitive impairments, particularly affecting executive functions. These impairments may result from the disease itself as well as from treatment with antiseizure medications. However, objective methods for the early detection and monitoring of cognitive side effects are still limited, especially in pediatric patients.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether eye-tracking and pupillometry can provide objective markers of cognitive functioning in children and adolescents with epilepsy. During the neuropsychological screening test EpiTrack Junior, eye movements and pupil responses will be recorded using an eye-tracking device. The study includes children and adolescents with epilepsy, patients after a first unprovoked epileptic seizure, and a healthy control group.

This monocentric prospective study combines cross-sectional and longitudinal assessments. Participants with epilepsy and healthy controls will undergo a single assessment, while participants after a first unprovoked seizure will be reassessed after 8–12 weeks. The study aims to improve understanding of cognitive changes associated with epilepsy and antiseizure medication treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children and adolescents with epilepsy or a first unprovoked epileptic seizure
- Healthy children and adolescents (control group)
- Written informed consent from legal guardians as well as assent/consent from participants according to age and capacity to understand
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient ability to cooperate or inability to complete the assessment as judged by the investigators
- Insufficient German language proficiency
- Known tonic or atonic drop seizures (clinical cohort only; safety aspect related to the eye-tracking device)
- Neurological disorders or chronic diseases involving the central nervous system (healthy control group only)
